title: PR benchmark harness with synthetic user traces for continuous regression gating
creator: Avery Chen
description: Replace the ad-hoc PR gating scripts with a deterministic, trace-driven benchmark harness that runs inside CI and evaluates tokens/sec and latency distributions against pinned baselines. The goal is to detect regressions introduced by PRs at merge time (or before) with low flakiness and clear rollback signals. This ticket covers harness design, synthetic trace generation, baseline storage, statistical regression tests (p95 tokens/sec and p95 latency), and PR integration (blocking and non-blocking modes).
motivation: Current CI checkpoints occasionally miss subtle throughput regressions or flag noisy false positives. We need a reproducible harness that mirrors production request mixes and reports actionable metrics in PRs so engineers can quickly understand perf impact before merging.
acceptance_criteria: CI job that runs a 3-minute trace-driven benchmark for PRs touching runtime or model serving paths
Baselines stored per-model + sequence-length-profile and retrievable by CI job
Regression detection uses robust statistical test (non-parametric bootstrap or permutation with suitable alpha) to compare p95 tokens/sec and p95 latency against baseline
PR comment/report contains concise result: pass/fail, delta percentages, CI 95% confidence intervals, and link to full dashboard run
False-positive rate under synthetic no-change runs < 3% over 100 runs
Support for opt-in 'experimental' gating mode (comment-only) and enforced blocking gating for release branches
measurement_methodology: Use deterministic synthetic traces derived from production samples (anonymized) plus fuzzing for sequence lengths. Each CI run executes N warmup iterations followed by M timed iterations. Aggregate per-step tokens and latencies, compute per-run distributions, then compare the p95 of tokens/sec and latencies to stored baselines using bootstrap-derived confidence intervals and a two-sided test. Runs are executed inside a pinned Docker image to minimize host variance.
design_decisions: Run lightweight, short-duration traces (2–5 minutes) to keep CI latency acceptable while preserving signal
Pin host CPU/GPU configuration in ephemeral CI runners via container resource limits and a known Docker base image
Store baselines in an immutable S3 path keyed by model, runtime commit tag, and trace-profile; baseline update requires a reviewed PR
Use statistically conservative thresholds (e.g., require >5% degradation AND statistically significant at alpha=0.01) to reduce false positives
Provide both 'blocking' and 'informational' modes, with blocking enabled only on protected branches
implementation_steps: 1) Build trace generator library that replays token sequences with configurable concurrency and prompt diversity
2) Implement CI job template (GitHub Actions) that pulls appropriate baseline, runs harness inside pinned Docker image, and uploads run artifacts to performance dashboard
3) Add statistical comparison library (bootstrap + effect size) and result formatter for PR comments
4) Create baseline promotion workflow: reviewable PR that replaces baseline on green experimental runs
5) Integrate gating policy: comment-only on feature branches, blocking on release/* branches; admins can override with reason
6) End-to-end testing using no-op change runs and synthetic regressions to validate false-positive and true-positive rates
7) Roll out to runtime and serving repos, then expand to console and optimizer repos as needed
risks_and_mitigations: Flakiness due to CI host variability — mitigate by using pinned Docker images, resource limits, and requiring at least 3 independent runs before failing gating
Baseline drift when runtime improves — mitigate with manual baseline promotion workflow and automated anomaly detection to suggest baseline refresh
Long CI time — mitigate by short traces and running harness only for PRs that touch performance-sensitive paths
Gaming the baseline — mitigate by requiring review for baseline changes and logging baseline promotion events

notes: This ticket intentionally keeps run duration short to balance CI cost versus detection sensitivity. If we cannot meet true-positive detection for subtle (3–5%) regressions with 3-minute runs, we'll evaluate a hybrid approach: short CI run for quick gating plus nightly full-length benchmark sweeps.
